dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Friend! That we should meet means that fate has surely smiled upon you. Oh, I have an excellent business proposition for you. If I could just have a moment of your time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why do you merchant types always sound so suspicious?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Oh, come now, don't be like that. The integrity of a Liyue merchant is as steadfast as the Geo Archon themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No harm in hearing you out, I guess.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: It's simple. Every day you find me some basic items, and trade them in here for a box full of exciting little curios.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Even the worst boxes have precious metals inside them... in the form of Mora cast at the Golden House, no less.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay, but what's in it for you?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Oh, my business model is a little too complex to explain right now. But, if I have your consistent support in this business deal, then perhaps I will consider letting you in on how it works one day. Hahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: So, whaddya think? Interested?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can't hurt to try it out.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Ahh, I see you've willingly returned. That must mean you trust me, even if only a little.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's heard of scams that start like this though. They rope you in with all the benefits in the beginning, so you let your guard down and that's when they get ya!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Hahahaha, please! I don't rely on scams to make my Mora. I rely on my keen sense of business trends.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I was once a merchant of curios. Why curios you ask? Well, because logically speaking, the rarer something is, the more expensive it is.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well Paimon's super rare — there's only one in all of Teyvat! So, ah, where's the Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Ehehehe, something big is about to happen to our world. And what do you think is going to become scarce once that happens?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: What was it I was telling you about yesterday? Ahh yes, supply and demand.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: You should know, because of Mondstadt's Stormterror attacks, orchard production was affected and stocks are low. As such, we can expect the price of Mondstadt's wines and ciders to go sky-high, all across Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we know a thing or two about the Stormterror issue...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: So, let's see how well you can put two and two together. Tell me, why am I swapping out my curios for basic household items?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Because... the whole world is about to be destroyed!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Hahahaha.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: What was I mentioning yesterday?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah yes. Okay, so let's say the world really was on the brink of destruction — how would you even know that anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: That is one of a merchant's other talents. Not only must we read the market and act accordingly, so too must we have our connections.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I happen to be in the know about some very top secret intel. Intel which has come from none other than the economic authority that is the Qixing themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: So yesterday I was telling you about... ah, that's right. The Qixing's intel.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: The Qixing are the seven greatest merchants in Liyue, who govern over everything to do with our economy, so it goes without saying that their intel is very accurate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So just what is this intel then?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Stormterror has affected Mondstadt's agricultural production, whilst the Fatui have been getting rather imperious in Liyue and Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: According to confidential intel said to have come from Ningguang, Tianquan of the Qixing herself, the Qixing plan to break ties with the Fatui, and simply let Liyue bear the brunt of the economic impact.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: And when that time comes, the Qixing will be sure to make a pretty penny off the inflated price of everyday items.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But where would that leave the poor people of Liyue?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: No, no, no, this isn't right... The word about the rift between the Qixing and the Fatui should be out by now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Have you ever stopped to consider that maybe this "secret intel" of yours is being "leaked" to you on purpose?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: You mean, this is a ploy by the Qixing to control small and medium business owners?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Based on our interactions with others, it seems like you're the only one getting duped.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I... I've been scammed... by Ningguang...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're not going to ask me to return my stuff now, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Integrity is the cornerstone of being a merchant, so I won't go back on my word but... But... this is terrible...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, don't give up! You've still got a long life to lead!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: You're right. My heart wasn't in the right place. How could the Qixing ever turn their backs on the people of Liyue in order to make a profit? Those everyday items are a necessity for the people to just get by. No one should attempt to corner the market like that, and I shouldn't have allowed myself to go along with it.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Friend, you have seen with your own eyes my very rise and fall. Let my mistakes be a lesson for you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That lesson being... to not become a merchant?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm going to need some time to myself to think about what's happened. Business will at least continue to go on, but in the immediate sense that doesn't help me a whole lot...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Ah, hello. Do you need something?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm here to do some business.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: The items needed today are as such.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: <color=#FFCC33FF>I'm here for my Box o' Marvels...</color>

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Here you are: genuine goods at a pleasing price. Worst-case scenario, it'll top up your coin pouch.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm here to do some business.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I thought you'd already taken a Box o' Marvels for today? That said, feel free to inspect the others. You'll see I don't cheat any of my customers.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can you run me through your background again?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I'm Liben, and once upon a time I sold curios.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: But I've finally said goodbye to that now that I've made it enough to rub shoulders with the Qixing. No more Mr. Small-Time Merchant for me!

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: And that's why you and I are about to start doing business together, and both of us are going to make a handsome sum!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What kind of business?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Simple. You find me a few basic every items, cooking ingredients and the like, and then you trade them with me for a Box o' Marvels, full of all kinds of nice little treasures.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Keep in mind that I've filled these Boxes o' Marvels with the fortune I made in my time as a seller of curios. There's no booby prizes to be found here, and I treat all my customers the same.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Why box them up and turn it into a lucky draw, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: What can I say, people like a gift box. It just makes everyone a little more inclined to get involved.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you earn any money like this?

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: See, this is where the clever bit comes in.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: I have recently become privy to some highly confidential intel from the Qixing. It's tough times ahead for the whole of Teyvat, apparently.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: If I start stockpiling everyday essentials now, before long I'll be able to sell them off at much higher prices and make a huge profit.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: See you around.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm here for my Box o' Marvels...

dialogues.speaker: Liben
dialogues.text: Here you are: genuine goods at a pleasing price. Worst-case scenario, it'll top up your coin pouch.
